title: First Memphis Five date, Paramount, and the California Ramblers
summary: He made the Memphis Five's first date for Paramount, auditioned the California Ramblers there, and recorded them under about twenty pseudonyms. He mentions his diaries and the Harlem Nest club's influence.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No, I think I made their first date for them, and we then freelanced around. I think that the first date was for the Paramount Records, which was an independent company at the time.

1140 Broadway. In fact, I auditioned the original California Ramblers down at 1140 Broadway in the Paramount. And, of course, I made records for them under Ananda Plume by the original Ramblers, with Red Nichols and Jimmy Dorsey and Tommy Dorsey, and, of course, Adrian Rilline, who developed into the greatest bass saxophone player in the world. So we had a real team at that time, you know, with great stars. And, as I say, I think I used about 20 nom de plumes or more. And I think that, as far as recording is concerned, I think I've, as an independent orchestra leader and production man, I think I've made more records than any other individual.
Well, I think more than any other man also, you've confused the picture for the jazz historian who tries to follow all the places you've been.

Well, I had a team of research men here for weeks looking over my records and diaries and getting personnel for these dates that I had on payroll books from 1925 or 1926 on, you see. But prior to that, it was simply the diaries. I've got the diaries from 1919 on, you see. And they had a real holiday and field day. I understand that those are coming out in discography form in the various issues of magazines from time to time.
The record research. The record research, actually. You used mainly the New York men, didn't you?
Yes, yes. I don't remember any New Orleans men. We had a lot of good men in New York that were influenced greatly by the Harlem bands, you know.

Of course, our band, the boys used to, after getting off the California Ramblers Inn date, they used to hobnob down at the Nest, which was a famous nightclub. They had a big band down there, you know. And that's where they got a lot of their inspiration for jazz.
